name: refactor_makefile_pattern_rule
description: Consolidates three near-identical .o rules into one pattern rule
prompts: The Makefile has three near-identical rules (a.o: a.c, b.o: b.c, c.o: c.c) that each run the same compile command. Refactor it to use ONE pattern rule (%.o: %.c) with automatic variables ($< and $@) so adding a new source doesn't need a new rule. The `app` link target, CFLAGS, and clean target stay; the build behavior must be identical. Recipe lines stay tab-indented, and the three explicit .o rules must be gone (collapsed into the single pattern rule).

setup_files.Makefile:
CC = gcc
CFLAGS = -Wall

app: a.o b.o c.o
	$(CC) -o app a.o b.o c.o

a.o: a.c
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c a.c -o a.o

b.o: b.c
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c b.c -o b.o

c.o: c.c
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c c.c -o c.o

.PHONY: clean
clean:
	rm -f app *.o

test_setup_files.test_pattern.py:
import subprocess

r = subprocess.run(['make'], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=45)
assert r.returncode == 0, f'make failed: {r.stderr}'
out = subprocess.run(['./app'], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=15).stdout.strip()
assert out == '3', f'build behavior changed: ./app printed {out!r}, want 3'

src = open('Makefile').read()
# consolidation proof: the per-file explicit rules must be gone
import re
explicit = re.findall(r'^[abc]\.o\s*:', src, re.MULTILINE)
assert len(explicit) == 0, f'explicit per-file .o rules still present: {explicit}'
assert '%.o' in src and '%.c' in src, 'no pattern rule found'
print('PASS')

reference_solution.Makefile:
CC = gcc
CFLAGS = -Wall

app: a.o b.o c.o
	$(CC) -o app a.o b.o c.o

%.o: %.c
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

.PHONY: clean
clean:
	rm -f app *.o

files.Makefile:
CC = gcc
CFLAGS = -Wall

app: a.o b.o c.o
	$(CC) -o app a.o b.o c.o

%.o: %.c
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $@ -o $<

.PHONY: clean
clean:
	rm -f app *.o
